Incident Bot: :rotating_light: page fired — PD-3781 — High TLS handshake failure rate for public-api.redwood.ai (observed 5xx spikes across edge). Auto-escalating to on-call.
PagerDuty Bot: PD-3781 triggered (urgency: high). Assigned to Jordan (on-call).
Jordan (on-call): acked. I'm on it. first thing: is this global or region-specific?
Maya (SRE): I'm seeing spike in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 in our edge metrics. TLS handshake errors up ~320% since 03:05 UTC. LB target health shows many targets Unhealthy in us-west-2 target-group-arn: arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:...:tg/abc123
Sam (ENG-infra): looking at ELB: describe-target-health shows ~60% failing with "Health check failed" + backend SSL errors. AWS ALB health check uses HTTPS /healthz.
Lina (Support): support queue getting a handful of reports: users seeing "502 Bad Gateway" and some client logs show "TLS handshake failed" from mobile SDKs. Customer-impact: partial for API endpoints, increasing.
Jordan (on-call): timeline? any recent deploys or infra changes?
Sam (ENG-infra): we rotated a subset of hosts into the target group as part of yesterday's autoscaling config change — perhaps they pulled a wrong image. Checking deploys: last deploy to infra-services was deploy-2026-03-14-02:50 (ID: dpl-8842).
Maya (SRE): quick cert check: `aws acm list-certificates --region us-east-1` shows cert arn:acm:... valid until 2027. Not an ACM expiry. Running `openssl s_client -connect public-api.redwood.ai:443 -servername public-api.redwood.ai` against a failing edge IP:
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
139857...:error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number:/build/openssl/...
---
no peer certificate available
---
```
That suggests the frontend is not presenting a proper TLS stack (maybe HTTP plain on HTTPS port).
Jordan (on-call): that aligns w/ nginx error traces I saw in recent logs: `SSL_do_handshake() failed (SSL: error:1408F119:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number)` on several new nodes.
Sam (ENG-infra): pulling a sample failing host: i-0a1b2c3d — ssh in: the private container running envoy appears to have config pointing to `/etc/ssl/certs/dev-selfsigned.pem` unexpectedly. This looks like a configuration drift during image build.
Maya (SRE): confirmed. The image tag used by ASG for the new instances references `infra-edge:latest` which accidentally pointed to `infra-edge:staging` yesterday. That image indeed bundles a self-signed cert.
Jordan (on-call): OK root cause likely bad image with self-signed certs landed on production ASG -> ALB health checks failing -> TLS handshake errors -> 502s. Scope: subset of targets in us-west-2 and eu-west-1; global traffic partially affected.
Lina (Support): current estimated affected customers: 8% of request volume for public-api endpoints. Tickets coming in from top-10 customers.
Jordan (on-call): mitigation options: 1) remove bad targets from target group (fast), 2) shift traffic to fallback ALB / old ASG, 3) rollback ASG launch config to earlier image. Which is fastest?
Ops_Tier2: removing targets is fastest. We can set desired capacity down for the misbehaving ASG to avoid new instances. Also we should coordinate with DNS only if we need to change routing — prefer in-place target removal to avoid DNS propagation delays.
Sam (ENG-infra): I'm removing the three known bad instance IDs from tg (aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn ... --targets Id=i-0a1b2c3d). Doing that now.
Incident Bot: target-deregistration: i-0a1b2c3d -> draining, i-0f4e5g6h -> draining.
Maya (SRE): watching graphs — TLS error rate dropping in us-west-2 already from 03:18 UTC. Edge latency also improving.
Jordan (on-call): support, post an interim public update? Lina?
Lina (Support): posted status: "Partial API errors — engineers investigating. Workaround: retry after a few seconds."
Lina (Support): customers asking for RCA; will collect incident timeline after fix.
Sam (ENG-infra): also patching ASG launch configuration to pin image to `infra-edge:2026-03-10-rc1` and rolling update to ensure new instances have correct cert. Running `aws autoscaling update-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name prod-edge-asg --launch-configuration-name lc-20260310`
Jordan (on-call): good. Any DNS involvement? I see one recent Route53 change yesterday for apex -> CDN alias to support new NLB but TTL was 60s so propagation already done. No need to change DNS.
Maya (SRE): verifying health across regions; eu-west-1 also returning to normal as deregistrations finish.
PagerDuty Bot: PD-3781 acknowledged by Jordan (on-call) at 03:20 UTC.
Jordan (on-call): will schedule on-call handoff in 40m. Ops_Tier2, please monitor for 30m post-deregistration then we can close if stable.
Ops_Tier2: monitoring. Setting alert suppression for PD-3781 to avoid noisy escalations while we stabilize.
Maya (SRE): logs show no TLS errors for last 10m from removed instances; ALB target healthy count back to 90% in both regions.
Lina (Support): support volume dropping. CS chimed: major customers report recovered.
Jordan (on-call): preparing short incident summary for postmortem: root cause = mis-tagged image pushed to production ASG containing self-signed cert; detection = ALB health checks + TLS handshake errors; mitigation = deregister bad targets, rollback launch-config, pin images; next steps = add CI gating to prevent staging tags on prod images, add image signature verification on deploy.
Incident Bot: scheduled postmortem meeting created — pm-incident-3781 on 2026-03-15 10:00 UTC.
Jordan (on-call): handing off to Maya at 03:40 UTC for monitoring window. I'll update PD when I leave.
Maya (SRE): taking over. I'll keep watch for an hour and start the RCA doc.
Jordan (on-call): thanks all. Marking PD as resolved if no regressions.
PagerDuty Bot: PD-3781 resolved by Jordan (on-call) at 03:45 UTC.
Maya (SRE): final check: confirm ALB cert chain OK, target groups healthy, no more self-signed certs. All good from my side.
Lina (Support): posting final customer note: "Service restored. Root cause under investigation. We will follow up with full RCA."
Jordan (on-call): closing thread; will add timeline & logs to postmortem doc. Good job team. :tada:
